deities: Lord Hrishikesh Narayan (Vishnu, carved from a single Shaligram stone)
Shri Bharatji Maharaj (the temple's namesake; regarded as a form of Vishnu)
Sri Yantra (installed above the main idol)
Mahadev and Bhadrakali shrines (in the complex)
festivals: Basant Panchami (grand annual procession; the idol is taken to Mayakund/Ganga for a holy bath and symbolically reinstalled)
Akshaya Tritiya (108 parikramas around the temple with the Lord's feet uncovered - believed equivalent to a Badrinath pilgrimage)

history.period: 8th-9th century CE (traditional founding by Adi Shankaracharya; present structure 1832 CE)
history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: this is the famous Bharat Mandir of Rishikesh's old town at Mayakund, the city's oldest and most sacred temple, dedicated to Lord Hrishikesh Narayan (Vishnu), whose black Shaligram-stone idol is carved from a single piece of holy stone. A Sri Yantra with nine interlocking triangles is installed in the inner dome above the idol. Tradition (Kedarkhand / temple accounts) holds that Adi Shankaracharya founded the temple in the 8th-9th century and reinstalled the deity on Basant Panchami (789 AD per the Rishikesh visitors' guide; '8th century' per other accounts - DATE CONFLICT FLAG: several travel guides say '12th century' instead; treat 8th-century founding as traditional, unverified claim). The name comes from Shri Bharatji Maharaj, not to be confused with Rama's brother Bharat (some accounts conflate them - flagged). Legend connects the site to Raibhya Rishi's penance, Bhakta Prahlad, and the Pandavas' journey to heaven. The original shrine was destroyed by Timur c. 1398 AD; the present structure was rebuilt in 1832 by Maharaja Yashwant Singh of Nabha. A small museum in the premises displays sculptures, pottery, bricks and coins found in excavation; just opposite the entrance stands a huge old tree of three intermingled roots representing Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh. Local lore claims Ashoka converted an early shrine here into a Buddhist monastery and that Buddha visited - flagged as unverified.

name: Bharat Mandir
town_description: Bharat Mandir stands at Mayakund on Ghat Road in the heart of old Rishikesh, near Triveni Ghat on the Ganges. Mayakund is one of the oldest quarters of the city, in the Rishikesh market area.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun (approx. 19-24 km; sources differ)
travel.road: In the heart of Rishikesh city at Mayakund / Main Bazar Road, near Triveni Ghat; easily reached by shared auto, cycle rickshaw or on foot from the old city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for weather; Basant Panchami (February-March) for the grand annual procession; Akshaya Tritiya for the 108-parikrama ritual
